source.title: From Circuit Evidence to Mechanistic Theory: An Inductive Logic Approach
source.authors: N. Aljaafari; Danilo S. Carvalho; André Freitas

page_placements.theme: Cross-model and cross-language comparisons show partial correspondence
Structural reproducibility depends on sampling and representation

record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes IOI circuits in other models using EAP-IG, attribution profiles, and circuit ablation. These are different methods and models from the GPT-2 small circuit study, but its results bear on cross-model IOI mechanisms and their causal contribution.
record.gate_note: The study cites Wang et al. (2023) for the GPT-2 small IOI circuit and uses its known sub-components as context; those cited findings are not treated as this study's results. It does not report a new test of GPT-2 small's 26 heads, seven classes, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. It reports its own IOI circuit results in Pythia and LLaMA, including circuit ablations and prompt-split structural comparisons. General comparisons of ILP with graph and feature baselines are not rows because they measure the study's representation method, not the IOI mechanism itself.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a methods paper on ILP representations of circuits. It does report its own IOI circuit results in Pythia-14M, Pythia-1B and LLaMA-3.2-1B: circuit-ablation ΔT, attention share, and faithfulness and DLA in Table 1. These bear on whether an IOI circuit carries the task in other models (V3) and on whether the circuit's apparent completeness depends on the metric (V5). It never identifies the original head classes and never examines GPT-2 small, so it is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that IOI is implemented by attention-mediated copying, structurally distinct from MLP-mediated semantic-role binding, and that this distinction holds across Pythia and LLaMA. They add that the IOI circuit's causal contribution flips sign from Pythia-14M to 1B. They frame transfer as candidate retrieval followed by behavioural and causal validation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses EAP-IG circuits with k=200 edges and three integrated-gradient steps, then computes direct-logit-attribution and attention-role profiles and evaluates circuit ablation. It does not reproduce the GPT-2 small circuit-finding and evaluation procedure or test its stated 26-head/seven-class faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI circuit-level causal contribution changes across model scale/family and across prompt-split circuits; the Pythia-14M primary and split results are negative while the reported Pythia-1B and LLaMA primary results are positive. Prompt-split structural consistency also differs by model.

fits_no_version.finding: IOI circuits found from disjoint random prompt splits are structurally more similar to each other than to other tasks' circuits in Pythia-1B (1.8×) and LLaMA (2.3×), but not in Pythia-14M (≈1.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit topology found by EAP-IG is stable across random prompt subsets of the same dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The dominant linguistic role of tokens attended by IOI circuit components shifts from object at 14M to function at the 1B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit attention relocates from name tokens to structural tokens with scale.

fits_no_version.finding: ILP-signature transfer retrieves IOI-matching candidates in Pythia-1B (8/41 accepted).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structural signatures of IOI circuits support cross-model candidate retrieval.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code and supplementary materials are available at an anonymized-for-review location)
record.problems: The evaluation uses only three models and a limited set of task families; the IOI circuits are derived using EAP-IG rather than a replication of the original GPT-2 small circuit analysis. Some IOI results are aggregate means across three prompt splits, and the study does not report the original head classes or directly compare ablation protocols. The paper itself notes that thresholds are empirically chosen, broader sensitivity analysis is limited, and greedy minimality may miss non-contiguous minimal subcircuits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI-specific circuit results relevant to the listed versions were omitted. Aggregate random-subgraph control summaries and results for other task families were not included as rows because they do not give separate IOI-specific outcomes for the claim.

untested.parts: All of it: GPT-2 small is not examined, and the 26 heads, 7 classes and faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria are not tested.
All of it: no name-mover ablation and no backup or self-repair analysis.
Identity of the head classes and roles (duplicate-token, S-inhibition, name-mover), training checkpoints, and reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
All of it: only EAP-IG is used, with one ablation type, and no circuit-recovery comparison is made.
Ablation-type variation and prompt-distribution variation; only the metric disagreement is shown.
All of it: name orders, templates and more names are not varied; the splits are disjoint subsets of one dataset.

missing.what: Causal vs marginal component counts for IOI by DLA: 26/0 (Py-14M), 34/2 (Py-1B), 0/29 (LLaMA).
Pythia-1B IOI circuit has 85 attn→attn edges, and LLaMA 44, forming three-hop attention chains.

record.verdict_notes: Wang et al. is cited only as background; this study is not an original source. ΔT is defined as an accuracy difference, yet its values exceed 1, so the units are unclear. Appendix F's '71–76% other-dominant' for IOI contradicts Table 1's object/function dominance. No check is reported that Pythia-14M can do IOI at all, so its null circuit result may reflect model incapacity. The prompt splits are disjoint subsets, not different templates, so they do not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: The GPT-2 small circuit, its 26-head/seven-class composition and roles, and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
The study does not ablate main name-mover heads or test backup-head self-repair.
It does not test the same named head classes and roles as the GPT-2 small circuit, training checkpoints, or reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
The study uses EAP-IG; it does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics for recovery of the same circuit.
It reports variation in circuit-level causal contribution across models and prompt splits, but does not compare ablation types or systematically vary evaluation metrics.
It compares circuits from disjoint prompt subsets, but does not separately test name orders, templates, or sentences with more names.

rows.subject: Pythia-14M
rows.operation_detail: Ablate the IOI circuit and compare task performance with the unablated model.
rows.note: The text describes the Pythia scale change from −0.91 to 4.37 as a sign reversal in the IOI circuit's functional role.
rows.check: The authors call this a sign reversal, but App. H.5 lists the 14M IOI circuits as non-significant against size-matched random subgraphs, so the state is absent, not reversed. It is a cross-model result, not ablation or metric sensitivity, so V5 is removed. It also conflicts with the Table 1 faithfulness of 0.79 for the same circuit.
